body.statement: If the entries of \(P\), \(c\), and a queried \(\Delta\) are real algebraic, then membership in either \(\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\) or \(\Theta_{+}(P)\), projection onto \(c\) or \(\Delta\), the algebraic endpoint values, and their inclusion flags are decided by a terminating real-closed-field quantifier-elimination procedure applied to the principal-minor form of the finite lift.
body.justification: Principal minors and real-closed-field elimination decide exact feasibility and projection on every algebraic observed-law face.
body.gap: Finite algebraic endpoint values require a nonempty fixed-slope fiber; the revised statement makes this premise explicit.
body.consumer: It supplies exact solver benchmarks without support or slope grids.
body.proof_tex:
For \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), let \(z_{\mathrm w}=(m,a,b)\) and \(z_+=(m,a,b,t)\).  Denote by
\[
 \Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)
\]
the conjunction of \(c>0\), the sixteen cell equalities, the APE equality with value \(d\), and every matrix inequality in \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}principal\text{-}minor\text{-}psd}\), each matrix inequality is equivalent to nonnegativity of its finitely many principal minors.  The coefficients of \(A_{xz,yw}\) and \(N_c\) are polynomials with integer coefficients in \(c\), while entries of \(H_s\), \(K_s\), and \(R_s\) are affine in the lift variables.  Thus \(\Phi_v\) is a first-order ordered-field formula with parameters given by the entries of \(P\).  No logarithm occurs: \(c\) is the slope-odds coordinate, with structural slope recovered deterministically as \(\log c\).

For every probability vector \(P\), including one on the boundary of the simplex, \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\) gives
\[
 (\log c,d)\in\Theta_v(P)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v). \tag{1}
\]
If \(P,c,d\) are real algebraic, the sentence on the right has real algebraic coefficients.  The terminating procedure in \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}elimination}\) converts it to a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions, and signs at real algebraic arguments are decidable.  This decides exact membership, including singular PSD faces because only weak polynomial inequalities are used.

The two coordinate projections are represented by
\[
 \{c:\exists d,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\},
 \qquad
 \{d:\exists c,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\}. \tag{2}
\]
The constraint \(c>0\) is already part of \(\Phi_v\).  Eliminating the quantified variables terminates and returns an exact finite Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions for either projection.  It also detects the empty set.

Fix algebraic \(P\) and algebraic \(c>0\), and suppose the fixed-\(c\) fiber is nonempty.  A real number \(\ell\) is its lower endpoint if and only if
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Inf}_v(\ell)\;:\!\Longleftrightarrow{}&
 \bigl[\exists d,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall d,z_v\,\{\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\Rightarrow \ell\le d\}\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall\varepsilon\,\{\varepsilon>0\Rightarrow
 \exists d,z_v\,[\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\wedge d<\ell+\varepsilon]\}\bigr].
 \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
Similarly, \(r\) is the upper endpoint if and only if
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Sup}_v(r)\;:\!\Longleftrightarrow{}&
 \bigl[\exists d,z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall d,z_v\,\{\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\Rightarrow d\le r\}\bigr]\\
 &{}\wedge
 \bigl[\forall\varepsilon\,\{\varepsilon>0\Rightarrow
 \exists d,z_v\,[\Phi_v(P,c,d,z_v)\wedge r-\varepsilon<d]\}\bigr].
 \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
Finiteness and uniqueness of both values follow from \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}slope\text{-}endpoints}\).  Quantifier elimination applied to (3) or (4) gives an exact semialgebraic description, over the field of real algebraic numbers generated by \(P\) and \(c\), of a singleton.  After identically zero polynomials are discarded, some polynomial in that description must vanish at the singleton: if none vanished, all polynomial signs would be locally constant and the described set would contain a nondegenerate interval.  Hence each endpoint is real algebraic, and the elimination output is an exact algebraic specification of it.

Finally, lower and upper inclusion are the separate sentences
\[
 \exists z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,\ell,z_v),
 \qquad
 \exists z_v\,\Phi_v(P,c,r,z_v). \tag{5}
\]
Their equivalence to model-side inclusion follows from (1), and they are precisely the tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\).  Applying the same terminating elimination procedure decides both flags.  This proves membership, projection, nonempty-fiber algebraic endpoint values, and separate attainment decisions without support or slope grids, including for boundary observed laws.
